newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS MONDAY WEAKER UNDER PRESSURE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR ENDS MONDAY WEAKER UNDER PRESSURE.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar was quoted weaker against major units at the close of business on Monday, pressured down by increased demand for foreign currency.
Exchange dealers said the central Reserve Bank only came into the the market in the morning with U.S. dollars, managing only to soften the local unit's fall.
"We had hoped the central (Reserve) bank would come in (again later) to support the dollar but they didn't. Probably they are happy with its current levels," one exchange dealer commented.
"I foresee a further depreciation in the coming week," he added.
"(But) it was a steady fall, so no-one is going to panic about it," another dealer said.
The Zimbabwe dollar closed on Monday at 10.9975/11.0075 against the U.S. dollar, down from 10.9700/9800 on Friday and was also weaker against sterling at 17.9455/9730 compared to 17.8800/9000.
It was at 6.6500/6585 from 6.5900/6100 against the mark and at 2.4940/4980 versus the rand against 2.4700/4900 last week.
